distribution.reason: Local SWToken candidate. CPL distributor source-access terms, actual-layer/generated-content review and digest-bound source-companion delivery remain incomplete; checker/consumer/proxy admission is separate.

constraints: Linux amd64/glibc 2.41, SWToken only. All hardware tokens, p11sak, ASan, s390x and FIPS claims are excluded. No upstream source patches.

Both channels dynamically link Debian OpenSSL 3.5.7 libcrypto.so.3 and require its packaged legacy provider. No from-source OpenSSL is needed. Basic runtime has provider/API, SWToken, pkcsslotd, libc/dl adapter, base libraries and exact liblber/NSS wrapper bytes.

Use a non-root caller UID with primary GID 1001. Immutable root:1001 strength.conf stays mode 0640, preserving native policy checks; NSS wrapper supplies the native p11lab account for that UID. The installed runner currently uses the host UID/GID, so its host primary GID must be 1001. Other primary groups are not qualified.

Bind writable /var/lib/p11lab; private ephemeral /run/p11lab and private container IPC/PID namespaces are required. Never share IPC with another runtime. Each shard/client owns a separate volume, container and daemon.

Persistent opencryptoki/opencryptoki.conf and complete are exact-byte validated. strength.conf is the sole declared symlink to immutable /usr/share/p11lab/opencryptoki/strength.conf. Data lives in opencryptoki/lib/opencryptoki/swtok/{NVTOK.DAT,MK_SO,MK_USER,TOK_OBJ}; HSM_MK_CHANGE remains empty. No system /etc/opencryptoki or /var/lib/opencryptoki state is used.

P11LAB_LABEL defaults to P11Lab, 1..32 ASCII letters/digits/spaces/dot/underscore/hyphen. Caller user/SO PINs are 4..8 bytes; first init requires both. The native factory SO PIN is replaced through C_SetPIN; selecting that factory value is refused. No baked caller credentials or initialized token data.

First init calls native C_InitToken(factory), SO login, C_SetPIN(caller SO), C_InitPIN(caller user), logout/close/finalize. Caller PINs travel over a bounded private stdin pipe, never native argv, logs or markers. Compatible repeated init preserves state and ignores changed credential files.

init/health/exec supervise native pkcsslotd for that operation only. Subreaper adoption of its native fork, verified child PID, readiness socket plus real native token check, volume/control leases, daemon-death detection, signal forwarding, bounded logs and bounded terminate/kill/reap prevent owned daemon orphans. exec retains the daemon for the complete application lifetime and preserves argv/status.

No persistent server/server-ready service is needed: preferred proxy daemon is launched through the same supervised exec. Lease serializes entire operations across containers sharing a volume; no parallel clients against a single state. No silent reset or retry of native state-changing calls.

Unknown/hidden entries, unsafe links/hardlinks, changed non-secret configuration, missing/incorrect-sized token files and busy init are refused before native open. Failures retain partial state for investigation. Reset requires caller removal/replacement of disposable state after all operations stop.

The general-token profile is retained after native P-256 independent verification and altered-message rejection in both channels; wider mechanisms, multi-client concurrency, power-loss recovery, other architectures/libcs/groups and provider-wide qualification are not asserted.

Installed checker smoke is blocked: the shared checker launcher drops trusted NSS/preload environment, producing native initialization 0x6 and zero completed observations. Preferred proxy crypto succeeds, but shared proxy post-health opens a second runtime before stopping the live daemon and is refused by the required volume lease. These are owning-launcher follow-ups, not provider workarounds.

All runtime/consumer/checker/proxy artifacts remain unreviewed for distribution. Preserve exact CPL provider source plus per-file terms, Debian closure sources/notices and generated build inputs; source admission, public delivery and publication are separate gates.
